senses.definition: To put something over another thing or hide it from view.
senses.example: Cover the bowl so the food stays fresh.

senses.definition: To include or deal with a subject.
senses.example: The second chapter will cover clouds and rain.

senses.definition: Something that goes over another thing to protect, hide, or close it.
senses.example: The cover of the book had a picture of a train.

senses.definition: A narrow split or opening in a surface.
senses.example: A tiny ant came out of a crack in the wall.

senses.definition: To split, make a sharp noise, or solve a hard problem.
senses.example: I managed to crack the code before the timer beeped.

senses.definition: A round hollow, often made where something struck a surface or around the opening of a volcano.
senses.example: The large crater on the Moon has high sides.

senses.definition: A marked line on a cricket pitch used to show a position or boundary in play.
senses.example: The batter ran past the crease before the ball reached the wicket.

senses.definition: To make something new or cause something to exist.
senses.example: We used paper scraps to create a city map.

senses.definition: A gradual increase in loudness in music.
senses.example: A slow crescendo took the tune from quiet to loud.

senses.definition: Growing different kinds of crops on the same land in a planned order, often to keep soil healthy and reduce pests.
senses.example: As part of their crop rotation, the farmers planted beans in a field that had grown corn the year before.

senses.definition: A large group of people in one place.
senses.example: A crowd gathered to watch the show.

senses.definition: To fill a place or press close together in it.
senses.example: Please don’t crowd around the doorway.

senses.definition: A part of a vehicle made to bend in a crash to help protect the people inside.
senses.example: A car can have a crumple zone near its front end.

senses.definition: To make a loud, crisp sound by chewing, crushing, or stepping on something.
senses.example: Dry leaves crunch beneath my boots.

senses.definition: A crisp sound made when something is chewed or crushed.
senses.example: I heard the crunch of gravel under the tires.

senses.definition: A solid with particles arranged in a pattern that repeats throughout it.
senses.example: Under a magnifier, a crystal of table salt looked like a tiny cube.

senses.definition: The space taken up by a cube whose edges are all one unit long.
senses.example: If one cube holds one cubic unit of space, three cubes hold three cubic units.

senses.definition: Broken or crushed glass gathered for use when making new glass.
senses.example: The glass plant mixed clean cullet with sand and its other supplies.

senses.definition: A small container for drinking, or an amount measured with a standard measuring cup.
senses.example: We poured a cup of water into the bowl.

senses.definition: To make a curved shape with your hands or hold something in that shape.
senses.example: She cupped a hand around the marble so it would not fall.

senses.definition: A soft lump of milk solids that can form when milk proteins gather together.
senses.example: The cheese maker gathered the curds into a mold.

senses.definition: Something that makes an illness or problem go away.
senses.example: The book describes how scientists look for a cure.

senses.definition: To make an illness go away or make food last longer by treating it.
senses.example: The book explains how people cure some foods with salt.

senses.definition: Wanting to know or find out about something.
senses.example: I was curious about how the clock could tell time.

senses.definition: Unusual in a way that makes you wonder about it.
senses.example: There was a curious mark on the underside of the stone.

senses.definition: The kind of money used in a country or shared by several countries.
senses.example: The yen is the currency used in Japan.

senses.definition: A flow of water or air in a particular direction.
senses.example: The river current carried the leaf past the bridge.

senses.definition: The rate at which electric charge moves through a path, such as a wire.
senses.example: When the switch closes, electric current can flow through the bulb.

senses.definition: Happening, used, or true now.
senses.example: The current plan is to meet after lunch.

senses.definition: A hanging piece of cloth that can cover a window or hide part of a stage.
senses.example: The curtain opened, and the first actor stepped forward.

senses.definition: A line or shape that bends smoothly.
senses.example: Trace the curve along the edge of the bowl.

senses.definition: To bend or follow a line that bends smoothly.
senses.example: The road curves around the hill.

senses.definition: Someone who buys goods or services from a person or business.
senses.example: Each customer chose one piece of fruit.

senses.definition: To split or remove something with a sharp edge.
senses.example: Please cut the paper along the dotted line.

senses.definition: To make an amount smaller or leave part of something out.
senses.example: We had to cut one scene from the play.

senses.definition: An opening made by something sharp, or a reduction in an amount.
senses.example: There was a small cut in the corner of the paper.

senses.definition: Using digital devices or online services to bully someone, such as by sending cruel or embarrassing messages.
senses.example: I showed a grown-up what had happened so we could report the cyberbullying.

senses.definition: A shape with two matching flat ends that are parallel, like the round ends of a can, joined by a side surface.
senses.example: The rolled-up poster formed a hollow cylinder.
